title: 30-31. HIS LIFE IS BOUND UP WITH THE BOY'S

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'So now, if the boy is not with us when I go back to your servant my father, and if my father, whose life is closely bound up with the boy's life, sees that the boy isn't there, he will die. Your servants will bring the grey head of our father down to the grave in sorrow.'" — Gen 44:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"His life is closely bound up with the boy's life." What a beautiful description of a father's love. Jacob is old and frail, and his very survival is tangled up with the wellbeing of his son. Take the son away, and the father will not survive it.

Judah understands this, and he cannot bear to be the one who does it. Notice his words: "Your servants will bring the grey head of our father down to the grave in sorrow." He knows they would be the cause. He is not willing to be that man again.

But sit with that phrase a moment longer. A father whose life is bound up with his son's. There is one Father whose love for His Son is deeper than any human love, and yet He gave that Son up — willingly, deliberately, for people who were His enemies (Rom 5:8; Rom 8:32).

Jacob could not bear the thought of losing his son. God the Father knew exactly what it would cost, and did not spare Him. That is the measure of how much He wanted you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose wellbeing is your own life closely bound up with?
2. What does it cost you to consider that God gave up His Son for you?
3. How does the Father's love change the way you see your own worth?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You did not spare Your own Son but gave Him up for me. I can barely take in that love. Let it settle deep in my heart and change the way I live. Amen.
